newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK must not tighten control on flat sale - solicitor.
newsitem.headline: HK must not tighten control on flat sale - solicitor.

text.p: Hong Kong's government should not step up control over the sale of uncompleted flats, a lawyer for the Lands Department told a news conference on Saturday.

"There is a risk of going too far to interfere in the private market which is really not the nature of Hong Kong or the government to regulate the market to such a degree," said Tom Berry, principal solicitor of the Lands Department.
In the territory, developers often "pre-sell" residential flats before they are completed.
With the recent surge in property prices, some have suggested that the government should control the sale of uncompleted units to ensure adequate property supply.

The department's deputy principal solicitor, Don Kitchell, said the authority was unable to control the timing of the sale of uncompleted flats or to ban developers from holding up flats for release when prices become higher.
"It's difficult for us to control their commerical decisions. They have to be responsible to their shareholders too," he said.
Berry said the department issued 36 consents to the pre-sale of 18,323 residential units in 1996.

"The majority of these units are estimated to be completed by the middle of this year. Some of them have already been put on sale in the market while the remainder are still in the hands of the developers," he said.
